title: Mathlib Imports for Euclidean Geometry
content: Imports five Mathlib modules: `Euclidean.Triangle` for triangle geometry, `Angle.Sphere` for angle measurement in inner product spaces, `Trigonometric.Basic` for `sin` and `cos`, `Tactic` for proof automation, and crucially `Archive.Wiedijk100Theorems.HeronsFormula` which provides the pre-proved `Theorems100.heron`.
mathContext: The Archive module provides `Theorems100.heron`: $\frac{1}{2}ab\sin(\angle p_1 p_2 p_3) = \sqrt{s(s-a)(s-b)(s-c)}$ for points $p_1, p_2, p_3$ in any real inner product space.

title: Namespace and Open Declarations
content: Sets `linter.unusedVariables false` (needed because `let` bindings in the main theorem trigger the linter), opens the `HeronsFormula` namespace, and brings `EuclideanGeometry` (for `angle`, `dist`) and `Real` (for `sqrt`, `sin`) into scope.
mathContext: Opening `EuclideanGeometry` provides `angle : P \to P \to P \to \mathbb{R}` measuring the angle at the second point, and `dist : P \to P \to \mathbb{R}` giving Euclidean distance.

title: Heron's Formula — Main Theorem (Wiedijk #57)
content: The central theorem: for vertices $p_1, p_2, p_3$ in any real inner product space with $p_1 \neq p_2$ and $p_3 \neq p_2$, the trigonometric area $\frac{1}{2}ab\sin(\angle p_1 p_2 p_3)$ equals $\sqrt{s(s-a)(s-b)(s-c)}$. The proof is a single application of `Theorems100.heron` from the Mathlib Archive.
mathContext: $\frac{1}{2} \cdot d(p_1,p_2) \cdot d(p_3,p_2) \cdot \sin(\angle p_1 p_2 p_3) = \sqrt{s(s-a)(s-b)(s-c)}$ where $s = (a+b+c)/2$. The theorem type signature uses `NormedAddCommGroup V`, `InnerProductSpace \mathbb{R} V`, `MetricSpace P`, `NormedAddTorsor V P` — maximally general for Euclidean geometry.

title: Semi-perimeter Definition
content: Defines the semi-perimeter $s = (a+b+c)/2$ as a noncomputable real-valued function. The semi-perimeter is half the perimeter and serves as the natural parameter for Heron's formula — each factor $(s-a)$, $(s-b)$, $(s-c)$ represents a complementary half-side.
mathContext: $s = \frac{a+b+c}{2}$, so $s-a = \frac{b+c-a}{2}$, $s-b = \frac{a+c-b}{2}$, $s-c = \frac{a+b-c}{2}$. These are non-negative precisely when the triangle inequality holds.

title: Heron's Product Definition
content: Defines the Heron product $s(s-a)(s-b)(s-c)$ as a noncomputable function using a `let` binding for $s$. This is the expression under the square root in Heron's formula. The product is a degree-4 symmetric polynomial in $(a,b,c)$.

title: Algebraic Expansion of Heron's Product
content: Proves $s(s-a)(s-b)(s-c) = \frac{(a+b+c)(-a+b+c)(a-b+c)(a+b-c)}{16}$ entirely by the `ring` tactic after unfolding definitions. This expanded form avoids computing $s$ and is numerically more stable for floating-point computation.

title: Alternative Expansion Ordering
content: An alternative ordering of the four factors in the expanded form: $\frac{(a+b+c)(a+b-c)(a-b+c)(-a+b+c)}{16}$. Algebraically identical but with factors reordered to group by sign pattern. Also proved by `ring`.
mathContext: Both orderings equal the same quartic polynomial $\frac{2a^2b^2 + 2b^2c^2 + 2c^2a^2 - a^4 - b^4 - c^4}{16}$; the reordering is purely cosmetic.

title: 3-4-5 Right Triangle Verification
content: Verifies that the Heron product for the 3-4-5 right triangle equals 36, giving area $\sqrt{36} = 6$. This matches the direct calculation $\frac{1}{2} \cdot 3 \cdot 4 = 6$. The product theorem uses `norm_num`; the area theorem uses `sqrt_sq` to simplify $\sqrt{6^2} = 6$.
mathContext: $s = 6$, so $6 \cdot 3 \cdot 2 \cdot 1 = 36$ and $\sqrt{36} = 6$. The 3-4-5 triple is the smallest Pythagorean triple ($3^2 + 4^2 = 5^2$).

title: Equilateral Triangle Verification
content: Verifies that an equilateral triangle with side 2 has Heron product 3, giving area $\sqrt{3}$. This matches the standard equilateral area formula $\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}s^2 = \sqrt{3}$. The area theorem uses `rw [heron_equilateral_2]` to reduce to `sqrt 3 = sqrt 3`.

title: 5-12-13 Right Triangle Verification
content: Verifies that the 5-12-13 right triangle has Heron product 900, giving area $\sqrt{900} = 30$. Uses `sqrt_sq` to simplify $\sqrt{30^2} = 30$. Matches the direct calculation $\frac{1}{2} \cdot 5 \cdot 12 = 30$.

title: Non-negativity from Triangle Inequality
content: Proves $s(s-a)(s-b)(s-c) \geq 0$ when the strict triangle inequality holds ($a < b+c$, $b < a+c$, $c < a+b$) and all sides are positive. The proof shows each of the four factors is strictly positive using `linarith`, then chains `mul_nonneg` three times.
mathContext: $0 < a, b, c$ and $a < b+c \Rightarrow s - a = \frac{b+c-a}{2} > 0$. Similarly for $s-b$ and $s-c$. Since $s > 0$ always, the product of four positive reals is positive (hence non-negative).

title: Triangle Area API
content: Defines a user-facing API function `triangle_area(a,b,c) = \sqrt{\text{heron\_product}(a,b,c)}` that computes the area directly from side lengths. Marked noncomputable due to dependence on `Real.sqrt`.

title: Triangle Area Non-negativity
content: Proves that `triangle_area` is always non-negative for valid triangles. The proof unfolds the definition and applies `sqrt_nonneg`, which holds unconditionally ($\sqrt{x} \geq 0$ for all real $x$, with the convention $\sqrt{x} = 0$ for $x < 0$).
